pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/1768

Mark, hope you don't mind a PR from an old contributor-- I ran into the absence of the `SERIAL`/`BIGSERIAL` pseduotypes when I was working on a fun little project to try porting all of the dbt-core integration tests over to use DuckDB instead of Postgres and figured that this was something I could knock it out myself w/o too much trouble (unlike, for example, adding transactional awareness to the ART index structure.) Please let me know if you're okay with the overall approach here (I took some liberties in terms of how things work in order to make the necessary changes as minimal as possible) and I will start aggressively adding unit tests for the new types. Thanks!
pr_comments: @Mytherin thanks for the feedback here, I will get on it! 💪

> @jwills any updates on this PR?

Hey Mark, apologies for the radio-silence, I got sick shortly after posting this and was then occupied by my day job and some dbt work. TL;DR I don't feel like I have a good way to add `SERIAL` support without some major surgery that I don't feel comfortable making-- re: my comment here: https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/3599#discussion_r869887506

For inspiration I went searching through the Postgres source code to see how they handled serial types, and it didn't seem to differ too-too much from my implementation (modulo the differences in the way that e.g. postgres stores constraints with the column instead of the table, default values are represented as constraints, etc., etc.):

Parsing/constraint generation for SERIAL: https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/master/src/backend/parser/parse_utilcmd.c#L532
nextval impl:
https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/master/src/backend/commands/sequence.c#L591

In particular, it read to me that they don't do binding on the sequence name in the function arguments, preferring lazy binding at some risk of a race condition and a performance penalty that they don't seem to care about too much.

Separately but relatedly, there's the issue of how the various SERIAL definitions would work with ALTER TABLE statements; my initial thought was to simply disallow them from ALTERs completely (since a SERIAL type always creates constraints.)

So yeah, feeling sort of stuck and currently inclined to just close this up and revisit it later.

Hey Josh, no worries. I just prefer not to leave PRs open for too long as they tend to drift. Thanks for the investigation - I think your implementation is close but still requires some ironing out. If you prefer we can close it up and you can revisit it later or somebody in our team can take over implementing this.

@Mytherin totally understand-- happy to hand it over to someone at the Labs if they're so inclined! I just think the design requires a higher-bandwidth channel than me and you across 10 timezones. ;-)
Fair enough. I am closing this for now then.

issue_context.title: Add support for SERIAL and BIGSERIAL type
issue_context.body: See [here](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.1/datatype-numeric.html). This is essentially a shortcut for creating a sequence, and assigning that sequence as the default value for the column.
comments:
I ran into this issue and stumbled across this thread. I'm experimenting with the unrelated-but-useful `sqlalchemy` dialect wrapper [`duckdb_engine`](https://github.com/Mause/duckdb_engine), and some of my tables use integer primary key columns. Under the `postrgresql` dialect, that translates to creating a column of type `SERIAL` (e.g. ```sqlalchemy.Column('id', sqlalchemy.Integer, primary_key=True)```).

 Because the `duckdb` SQL parser is based off the PostrgreSQL parser, the [`duckdb_engine` dialect inherits from the `postgresql` dialect](https://github.com/Mause/duckdb_engine/blob/cfc626e3274f80746d09d4585c5636c65b3afbc1/duckdb_engine/__init__.py#L52). Of course `duckdb` can't expect to cover all the features of PostgreSQL, but I think adding the `SERIAL` type wouldn't be too difficult.

When searching the `duckdb` source for the not implemented error, I came across [this line](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/57640e5c04fd0748532451b24e2001f1e17ac011/src/common/types.cpp#L484), which led me to diving into how `LogicalTypes` work. If there's interest, I could give a swing at trying to implement `SERIAL` / `BIGSERIAL`. It's about time I get over my impostor syndrome, and I really would like to contribute to other open source projects.

I think the best long term solution would be adding support for `SERIAL` in `duckdb`, but for the time being, avoiding `SERIAL` and using something else might be the best solution. Relying on an auto-incrementing column is convenient but missing support is not entirely a deal breaker.
@bmeares that would be amazing if you could do that, as I'd love to have that fixed in duckdb_engine

@Mause Thanks for hopping in, and thanks for putting together `duckdb_engine`. I was looking at your documentation and the [`sqlalchemy` docs for creating sequences](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/14/core/defaults.html#associating-a-sequence-as-the-server-side-default). From what I can tell, I can achieve the same result of a `SERIAL` column by passing a `sqlalchemy.Sequence()` object with the Column keyword argument `server_default=sequence.next_value()`. For example:

```python
>>> import sqlalchemy
>>> engine = sqlalchemy.create_engine('duckdb:////path/to/duck.db')
>>> metadata = sqlalchemy.MetaData(engine)
>>> user_id_seq = sqlalchemy.Sequence('user_id_seq')
>>> users_table = sqlalchemy.Table(
...     'users',
...     metadata,
...     sqlalchemy.Column(
...         'id',
...         sqlalchemy.Integer,
...         user_id_seq,
...         server_default=user_id_seq.next_value(),
...         primary_key=True,
...     ),
... )
>>> metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
```

I hadn't heard of `sqlalchemy.Sequence` until I saw it on your `duckdb` README. Is this a viable alternative to PostgreSQL's `SERIAL` type? The `sqlalchemy` docs state
> The following technique is known to work only with the PostgreSQL database. It does not work with Oracle.

but I was able to test it successfully with `duckdb`.

[I've opened a PR](https://github.com/Mause/duckdb_engine/pull/78) on the `duckdb_engine` repository to continue the discussion, and if I get anywhere with implementing `SERIAL` I'll post it here.

Thanks for the offer! Indeed offering all of Postgres' features is infeasible, but we should definitely add the SERIAL type for increased compatibility. As far as I understand it from Postgres, `serial`/`bigserial` are not actually real types. That is to say, this query fails:

```sql
-- ERROR:  type "serial" does not exist
select 3::serial;
```

Serial types can only be used in a `CREATE TABLE` statement, and are essentially an alias for attaching a sequence to a table and using that as a default value, e.g.:

```sql
CREATE TABLE integers(i SERIAL);
-- this statement is equivalent to
CREATE SEQUENCE __internal_serial_sequence_integers_1;
CREATE TABLE integers(i INTEGER DEFAULT(nextval('__internal_serial_sequence_integers_1')));
```

The second part already works in DuckDB, so all that is required is adding this "shortcut".

review_comments: This block is to ensure that the sequence that is associated with the SERIAL column is always dropped when the parent table is dropped; apparently the SERIAL sequences in Postgres are technically owned by the column (not the table), but I don't think DuckDB has a concept of column-level ownership of things yet.

This is where I played things fast and loose to make this work: before, this would throw an error if the sequence that the `nextval` function was expecting didn't exist, but since the impl of `nextval` already also supports the potential for its argument to not be a foldable expression, I could essentially cheat here and have this block of code set a `nullptr` for the `sequence` argument in case that the sequence that `nextval` will be calling doesn't exist at the time the function is bound.
Indeed ideally this is removed - particularly because if `sequence` is not set many catalog lookups will be performed, which will make insertions much slower.

So the bit I haven't figured out how to pull off is this: I'm defining the sequence and the `nextval` expression to use it as the default value for the ColumnDefinition during parsing, but the `nextval` function will be bound (and thus have its sequence catalog entry set) _before_ I am actually able to create the sequence in the catalog during table creation. Being lazy here (i.e., allowing for the catalog entry to not exist at the time of function binding) lets me get around this, but as you said, the performance hit of having to do this lookup over and over again while doing lots of inserts could well be substantial.

Is there a good way out of this puzzle?
(This is the exception you get from Postgres when you try to specify a default value for a SERIAL column type)

I created this b/c I needed some richer info passed back up the stack from the `TransformTypeName` function- I think it could also be a mechanism to implement the check constraints on varchar(n) types and I have some steps in that direction in this PR, but I'll obviously I'd be inclined to save the real work to implement those checks for a separate PR.

Check constraints for `VARCHAR(n)` columns can be quite easily created by just adding a `CHECK(LENGTH(col)<n)` constraint, no? Perhaps the `SERIAL` type can also be communicated back up the tree with a new constraint type `SerialConstraint` (or similar)?
